analysis.title: Bank Earnings Day 2 Wrap From Goldman's Fins Desk
key_insights: GS bank specialist Christian DeGrasse says the tape is choppy and driven by shifting concerns about macro and data centers. Bank stocks fell sharply in September and have fallen further in October despite mostly in-line earnings (Bank of America the exception).

DeGrasse says Financials often trade inversely to AI when AI rallies. When the market worries about the AI capex buildout and its funding, the link between Financials, capital markets and AI is reestablished.

Rates round-tripped the morning CPI print. Financials closed off the lows, but the tape is moving against stocks levered to economic growth. GS's long cyclicals vs defensives basket is down 6% from early October levels.
DeGrasse asks whether the rest of the market's cyclical exposure is catching up to what Financials and capital markets have signaled for a month.

Sentiment on bank earnings reactions is sharply negative, and investors are focusing on negative datapoints more than positive ones. DeGrasse calls it 'narrative piling on to price action' and says the desk struggles to find reasons for Citigroup's underperformance the day before.

Price action is questioning the level of earnings growth, not credit quality (see bank P/TBV multiples). Credit is close to the bottom of the list of debates, which are pipelines and capital markets backlogs, capital, operating leverage and margin levers.

BAC fell 5%. Feedback was that the quarter matched mid-quarter guidance on weaker trading and a lack of expense offset, but was worse than indicated. The stock was indicated down 8% pre-market, with a better 2027 NII guide failing to spark a rally.

BAC bulls focus on the NII upside story. Bears point to capital at 10.9% with GSIB pressure at the start of the new year, a possible slowdown in buybacks or balance sheet growth, and regulatory focus that may limit expense levers.

PGR fell 6% on slower growth and weaker margin in Personal Auto. Concerns were a slowdown in Direct (with a debate over whether agents are a factor) and worsening pricing, with agency/direct annualized premium per policy at -5.0%/-3.6%. Insurance specialists pushed back, calling the move an overreaction to a worse-than-expected monthly.

STT fell 6% on a top line miss from Asset Servicing and other fees, with NII and NIM slightly better. The implied 4Q guide was 5% below GS's estimate while the buyside expected upside. The stock was up 35% YTD at a premium multiple to its 5-year history going in.
MS fell 3%. Wealth pre-tax margin missed consensus by 30bps. The broader overhang is macro, rates and cycle, plus data center noise. The 3Q normalization in IB and Trading was better than feared.

BLK was flat after a strong quarter with next to zero pushback and desk crowding at 8/10. Organic fee growth was 11% vs a 8-9% bogey, and adjusted margin was 47.8% vs 45.9% last quarter and 44.5% the quarter before. Blostein estimates about 49% adjusted for performance fees.

market_movers.rationale: Stock fell 5% on earnings. Bulls cite the NII upside and 2027 NII guide. Bears cite capital at 10.9%, GSIB pressure and limited expense levers.
Stock fell 6% on slower Personal Auto growth, a Direct slowdown and falling premium per policy. Insurance specialists call it an overreaction.
Stock fell 6% on an Asset Servicing and fees top line miss and an implied 4Q guide 5% below GS's estimate, after a 35% YTD run.
Stock fell 3% on a 30bps wealth pre-tax margin miss and macro, rates and data center noise.
Stock was flat after 11% organic fee growth and adjusted margin of 47.8%, with no pushback.

sector_views.rationale: Bank stocks are weak in September and October on questions about earnings growth, with credit not the concern. They trade inversely to AI when AI rallies and react to AI capex funding worries.
GS's long cyclicals vs defensives basket is down 6% from early October levels, with a clear tilt toward defensive exposure.

earnings_insights: BAC reported 3Q with the stock down 5% on the day after being indicated down 8% pre-market. The quarter was worse than the mid-quarter guide on weaker trading and no expense offset. The 2027 NII guide was better, and CET1 capital is at 10.9%.
PGR reported monthly results worse than expected. Agency and direct annualized premium per policy were -5.0% and -3.6%. Stock down 6%.
STT reported 3Q with a top line miss from Asset Servicing and other fees, and NII and NIM slightly better. The implied 4Q guide is 5% below GS's estimate. Stock down 6%.
MS reported 3Q with wealth pre-tax margin 30bps below consensus. IB and Trading normalization was better than feared. Stock down 3%.
BLK reported 3Q with organic fee growth of 11% vs a 8-9% expected range and adjusted margin of 47.8% vs 45.9% last quarter. Stock flat.

risk_factors: Worry about the AI capex buildout and its funding could reconnect Financials with capital markets and AI weakness.
Credit could become a concern if debt backing data centers fails.
BAC capital inflexibility, GSIB pressure from the start of next year and regulatory limits on expense levers.
Slower revenue growth and operating leverage across banks.
PGR pricing deterioration and a Direct slowdown.
vol_and_positioning: GS desk crowding for BLK was 8/10 going into earnings.
Flows in the trust bank space have picked up, suggesting a real debate in the stocks. STT is one of the few financials pockets showing defense in the current tape.

tension_points.bull_case: The NII upside story is intact, with a better 2027 NII guide that should lift numbers.
tension_points.bear_case: Capital is at 10.9% with GSIB pressure at the start of the new year, so buybacks or balance sheet growth may slow, and regulatory focus may limit expense levers.

tension_points.bull_case: Insurance specialists call the move an overreaction to a worse-than-expected monthly, and say agents should help growth as a lower cost option, with any implications more likely on margin.
tension_points.bear_case: Direct is slowing, possibly because agents already play a part, and agency/direct annualized premium per policy is -5.0%/-3.6%.

tension_points.bull_case: Credit quality is not the debate, and price action is questioning earnings growth levels, not credit issues.
tension_points.bear_case: If AI capex funding worries persist, Financials stay tied to capital markets and AI weakness. Credit becomes a concern if data center debt fails.
